chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'ala, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who seizes the thief: is it better to leave him (the thief) or to raise (the matter) (to the Imam)? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed Sufyan ibn Umayyah was reclining in the Masjid on his cloak. He arose to urinate, and when he returned, his cloak had been taken. He sought its owner and found him, and brought him to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He (peace be upon him) said: "Cut his hand." Sufyan said: "O Messenger of Allah, I gift that to him." The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: "Why was that not done before you brought him to me?"'
He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about excusing (forgiving) regarding the fixed penalties before they reach the Imam, and he said: It is good.'

key_terms.صَفْوَانُ بْنُ أُمَيَّةَ: Sufyan ibn Umayyah, a companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Can a thief be forgiven before the case reaches the Imam in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the procedural timing of *afw* (forgiveness) in *hudud* cases, distinguishing between the victim's right to pardon before the case reaches the Imam and the subsequent judicial authority. The narrative of Sufyan ibn Umayyah highlights the Prophet’s emphasis on early resolution, while the Imam’s confirmation establishes that pre-imam forgiveness is not only valid but commendable (*hasan*), reinforcing the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding fixed penalties.
